<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **58** documentable anchor(s).

**53** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`, `objectName (symbol, 57 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **246** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **181** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **181**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **122** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **48** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c237c2ae789de57da2d1434427a3f131a9f57efd` — the merge of head `94b1978f553ebdbbb87c40a538004daec815f8ee` into base `7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c237c2ae789de57da2d1434427a3f131a9f57efd && git checkout c237c2ae789de57da2d1434427a3f131a9f57efd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4 94b1978f553ebdbbb87c40a538004daec815f8ee && git checkout -B drift-repro 7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4 && git merge --no-ff 94b1978f553ebdbbb87c40a538004daec815f8ee

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

That covered `unqualifiedHandler`, `pickActionHolder`, `bareRouteHolderRefusal`, `environmentStoredActionNames`, the `/meta` object-less refusal, `BUILT_IN_BARE_NAMES` and the item-1 delta. Contract review and ACCEPT are seat 1's. This is the first epic read since #32101 was superseded.

- **Red line 1, never loosen: holds.**
  - The engine refuses only in ruling 1's two cases: two packages on one key, or, on the object-less key, a package beside host code or a plugin. Everything else runs `actions.get(key)`, as on main.

- **Red line 2, never guess: holds** for every path this PR changes.
  - The bare REST door, MCP `run_action` and the engine answer `409` naming every holder.
  - Once the listing capability is present, a listing read that fails answers `503` and never falls back to a rung (F1).
  - A disabled package holds nothing (F4).
  - The by-name read's refusal is read as a refusal and never as degraded.
- **Red line 3, releasable: holds.**
  - With one holder, every door answers as before.
  - The changeset declares the narrowings with FROM→TO, including the item-1 in-process `get('action', NAME)` refusal and the F2 change to the environment's row.
  - The widening (two namespaces may each hold an object-less name) is declared.
  - First-party count is 0.
- **Item 1 (B-shape addition 1) is built.** `action` joins `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES`, with the in-process slot pins and the artifact-door dogfood. Seat 1 already accepted items 4 and 5. Item 2 rides #32198.

**Not charged to this head; carried by follow-up cards.** Seat 1 files them from `/mnt/project-files/epic-31527/31697-followups.md`.
1. **Card 1: a bare `GET /meta/action/NAME` for two packages' same-named actions on two different objects answers `200` with one of them.** On main it answered the survivor; at this head it answers the first registered. That is a pick, and it is live on main, so this PR does not introduce it. The changeset declares the change of which one is served. One cause is `getMetaItem` step 2's empty `catch`: it swallows the metadata service's refusal, and the registry then picks. The card refuses that read and rethrows a package-scoped refusal there. It also audits the other slotted types for the same swallow.
2. **Card 2: `composeStacks` still refuses two namespaces' object-less action of one name.** That fails closed. The card admits the pair so that compose matches install.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8cf8c844dda8d6c491a4fb778a529e3e21e8d750`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-action-slots.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-actions.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/bound-action-collision-report.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-bare-name-one-holder-ai-family.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-bare-name-one-holder-request-family.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/action-handler-owner-gates.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions-addressed-route.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-references.integration.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/action-slotted-store-artifact.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/bare-name-one-holder-request-family.dogfood.test.ts + packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-metadata-service-read.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-package-addressing.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-handler-coordinate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-compatibility-api.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/marketplaceApi.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (read in the PR tree or on `main`, not reviewed). Not reviewed: .changeset/31697-action-names-per-namespace.md (prose face; read for ②).

Inputs: card #31697 (body and all 12 comments, the os-dev-report 6767435396 among them), the superseded PR #32101's record 6762242732 and the epic records 6762108144 and 6762267053, PR #32213 (body, 18 files, the net diff against the merge base 0f7389cc on `main`), the check-runs on the head, and the #31527 thread through 6767570817. Nothing was built or run.

Gate verdicts on the head, as read: none. The head has 0 check-runs. Five check suites exist and all are `queued` with no conclusion. The PR is a draft and GitHub reports `mergeable_state: dirty`: `main` moved to 0eca80a7, and #32192 (e40f2df2) rewrote the line this PR edits in `packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts` (`main` now holds `api`, `agent`, `skill`; this head holds `api`, `action`). So no gate has judged this tree, and this tree cannot land as it is. A PASS on this head was not available whatever ④ found. The next head merges `origin/main` and keeps all four entries.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Install side: the object-less `action` joins `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES` (bare-name-one-holder.ts:288). Right. One entry in the shared switch, judged by `bareNameHoldersMeet`. A co-owner, a package with no namespace, base/system/sys and a built-in stay refused, each with a pin in the request-family test.
2. Engine: `unqualifiedHandler` (engine-actions.ts:320) refuses two packages on one key, and, on the object-less key only, a package beside host code or a plugin. Right, and it is exactly the scope of epic ruling 6762267053 item 1. Both #30542 pins are untouched in the diff. An environment-authored handler and a declared override are not counted as owners (`codeOwnerOf`, :343); I tried the override path and it holds, because the override binds at its base's coordinate.
3. MCP bare `run_action` and the bare REST door both answer through `pickActionHolder` (action-execution.ts:4784). Right for the two declared cases. The platform is counted only on the object-less key, as ruled.
4. Bare REST when the listing throws: 503, nothing run. Right in the shape the epic record 6762108144 prescribed. One added condition rests on a premise the tree does not support, finding G3.
5. `/meta/action/NAME` with no package, object-less: refused before any layer is read; a host item beside a package is the platform's and is refused naming both; a disabled package is no holder. Right.
6. Source classifier keyed by `OWNER:NAME` and `OBJECT:NAME`, legacy organization rows left out. Right.
7. `action` joins `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES` (package-slotted-store.ts:54). Wrong key for this type, finding G1.
8. `BUILT_IN_BARE_NAMES.action` holds `install_package`. It meets the letter of ruling 2 (b) and not its purpose, finding G6.
9. No public export is removed or renamed. Added: `environmentStoredActionNames`, `EnvironmentStoredActionNames` (runtime), `SchemaRegistry#refuseAmbiguousObjectLessAction` (objectql), an optional eighth parameter on `resolveActionByName`. Additive.

Findings of record 6762242732 on this tree: F1 fixed, subject to G3. F2 fixed and declared. F3 fixed. F4 fixed at `/meta` and at the declaration, not at the engine door, finding G4. F5 fixed. F6 closed: declared in body and changeset, and recorded on #31527 (6767570817). F7 answered by the built-in entry, see G6.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

The changeset moves `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` at `minor`. Against ruling A as `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` and AGENTS.md state it (the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone; a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves): the four packages are the four whose `src` the diff moves, `cli` and `qa/dogfood` change tests only, so `minor` on each is right, `@objectstack/metadata` included. The BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker (`not-required`, no-migration-prescription) are present. The PR body and the changeset carry the same two declaration lines. `Check Changeset` has not run on this head.

The kind token is wrong. `Metadata-protocol: added` was right on #32101, where the built-in set was empty. This head adds a refusal at the install door of a name an author could write (an object-less action named `install_package`). The fleet's own precedent calls an install-door name refusal `narrowed` (#30803, #31414, #31670 changesets on `main`), and the rule is "several: `narrowed` over `semantic` over `added`". The level does not move; the token decides the release-notes section. Should-fix (G5), on the body and the changeset. If G6 ends with the built-in entry removed, `added` stands.

Narrowings in the tree against their declaration (FROM, TO, first-party count):
- two packages on one key, bare call, four doors: declared, count 0. Complete.
- a package beside host code or a plugin on the object-less key: declared, count 0. Complete.
- object-less `install_package` refused at install: declared, "no first-party package declares it". The fix (rename) is not written. Nit.
- every bare `POST /actions/:object/:action` answers 503 while the listing cannot be read, one-holder names included: stated in a late paragraph of the changeset, outside the `Clause-②:` line and outside the BREAKING list. See G8.
- in-process `get` / `getDiagnosed('action', NAME)` with no package, for two packages' same-named actions on two DIFFERENT objects, is now 409: stated in the changeset, with no first-party count for that class. The census quoted (no object and name two holders answer; no owner-less declaration) measures same-key pairs. See G1.
- bare `GET /meta/action/NAME` for that same pair changes which body it serves (the last registered before, the first registered now): stated in the changeset as a fact, not as a narrowing, with no count. See G1.

### ③ Boundary flags

Size: about 1564 changed lines against the 3000 threshold. Inside.

The dev report's deviations and open questions (6767435396):
1. F1 "a capability counts as absent when the protocol's own engine registers no `sys_metadata` object": not accepted as written. Finding G3, escalated to the epic seat.
2. Forced test change, the two plane-down cases in `action-handler-owner-gates.test.ts` now expect 503: accepted. Epic record 6762108144 orders fail-closed, and the old pins asserted the fail-open answer. See G8 for how it is declared.
3. "Ruling 1 reaches the declaration doors too": accepted. It is the same scope applied at `pickActionHolder`, pinned by "the platform beside one package on an object-bound key is not refused".
4. Open question, two packages that both bind `install_package` to `sys_package` are refused by ruling A: not answered by any record I was given. Escalated to the epic seat with G6.
5. Console follow-up not recorded on #31527: answered. It is recorded (6767570817). The PR body's sentence that it is not is stale. Nit.
6. "A host (package-less) action item over a package-held name reads back as that package's overlay": accepted as ADR-0150 D4. The epic's open item 1 (6761813588) covers the two-holder case, and `refuseAmbiguousObjectLessAction` refuses it there.
7. B-shape additions 6766935846. Item 1 is built here; G1 is about how. Item 2 (removal by slot) is not built and rides #32198, which is still open; the epic ledger 6767570817 accepts that order. Item 4: `action` registers no redactor; accepted on the PR's statement, which I did not disprove. Item 5: built (F4), with G4.
8. `composeStacks` refuses two stacks' same object-less action key: finding G7.

Escalated to the epic seat, in one place: G1 (a refusal and a changed pick outside the two declared cases; the card says such a narrowing goes to the maintainer before landing), G3 (does a kernel with `environmentId` set register `sys_metadata`?), G6 with question 4 (ruling 2 (b)'s purpose).

The carry-in 6760055671 asks for a red-line review by the epic seat before landing. This record is not that review.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing itself is sound where it is declared. On the four bare doors it makes the spec's own refusal real (ADR-0150 D5: an ambiguous bare name answers 409 naming the candidates), the addressed doors reach each holder, and it takes no declared capability away at the consumer. The findings are about one place where the refusal now fires on names that do not meet, one place where it leaks, and what the patch round left half done.

**G1 — must-fix. The slotted store keys an action by `(package, name)`, and an action's identity is `(package, object, name)`.** The per-type table (6723462584) keys action as `objectName:name` plus package. `packages/objectql/src/action-package-addressing.ts` says it in its header: seen through one owner key, "two packages' `approve` on two objects are then two names that never meet". `package-slotted-store.ts:54` puts `action` under a rule written for `api`, `agent` and `skill`, whose name is their whole key. For an action the store's key drops the object. Three things follow, all read in the tree:

- (a) `MetadataManager.get` and `getDiagnosed('action', NAME)` with no package (metadata-manager.ts:1003, :1045, through `readStoreEntry`) answer the D3 refusal `ambiguous-in-environment`, naming both packages, for two packages that each bind `NAME` to their OWN object. Each key has one holder. That refusal is neither of the two cases epic ruling 6762267053 item 1 lists, and that ruling pulled back a refusal of the same standing (host code beside a package on an object-bound key) with a first-party count of 0. No count is given for this class at all.
- (b) At `GET /meta/action/NAME` the same refusal is thrown inside `readMetaItem`'s step 2 and swallowed by its `catch` (protocol-meta-item-reads.ts:581, commented "MetadataService not available — fall through"); step 3 then serves `registry.getItem`, the first registered (:616). The PR pins that as intended (action-slotted-store-artifact.dogfood.test.ts:142-152: "serves the first registered"). So one component judges the name ambiguous and names both, and the published door turns that into a first-registered answer. Red line 1 names exactly this ("no first-registered fallback ... no silent pick"), and red line 2 says ambiguity is reported, never guessed. Base picked too (the last registered); the change is that this head moves the pick and arrives at it by discarding a refusal. And it moves it for a state any multi-package deployment can already be in, which is what reading (b) of red line 3 forbids outside the declared narrowing. Console's 409 was accepted in ruling 2 because it appears only in a state this PR newly lets install; this does not have that property.
- (c) `getMetaItemLayered` swallows the same throw (protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts:189) and reads the registry. The bare layered read of a two-holder object-less name is not pinned anywhere in this diff. I could not settle by reading whether a gate upstream refuses it first.

The two doors also disagree about one name (in process 409, HTTP 200), and the PR's own CONTROL in `action-package-addressing.test.ts` ("two packages' actions of one name bound to two objects are not refused (object-bound reads are not this card's)") states the contract the store now contradicts. The fix is the store's to make: slot an action by its owner key as well (`standaloneActionOwnerKey`, the key every other reader in this epic uses), so two objects' actions never meet and the object-less pair still does; and stop reading a thrown `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` at step 2 as an absent service. Then the dogfood's fourth case pins "unchanged", not "first registered". One package binding one name to two objects (legal since the Q1 ruling 6724050556) falls into one slot today, as on base; the same re-keying fixes it. If the seat prefers to keep the name-only key, the 409 in (a) and the changed pick in (b) go to the maintainer first, as the card's acceptance says.

**G3 — should-fix, escalated. The third "capability absent" condition rests on "every served kernel registers `sys_metadata`", and the tree says otherwise in two places.** `bareRouteHolderRefusal` returns "judges nothing" when the protocol's engine has no `sys_metadata` schema (action-execution.ts:5726, `holdsMetadataStore` :5761). Epic record 6762108144 named two absent shapes (no service resolves; the listing is not a function). This is a third, added so the 28 bare-engine fixtures keep passing, and its docblock justifies it with "every served kernel registers it". But `ObjectQLPluginOptions` says a kernel with `environmentId` set "does not provision the metadata-storage platform objects locally" (objectql/src/plugin.ts:288), and `assembleMetadataProtocol` registers them only when `environmentId === undefined` (metadata-protocol/src/plugin.ts:228). If such a kernel's engine answers no schema for `sys_metadata`, the bare REST door judges nothing there and the rungs serve the object's own declaration for a same-object pair: the F1 leak, in the per-environment topology, where multi-package installs live. I cannot tell from this repository whether the cloud assembly registers the object by another path. The dev should show it (a pin on a kernel built with `environmentId`, or the registration cited), or drop the third condition and fix the 28 fixtures. Also: on the same bare-engine composition MCP's bare call throws on the listing while REST judges nothing, so the two bare doors disagree there.

**G4 — should-fix. A disabled package is still a holder at the engine door.** The changeset says "a disabled package holds nothing at these doors: beside it, the enabled holder answers". That is true of `/meta` and of the declaration the REST door resolves. It is not true of `executeAction`: `SchemaRegistry.disablePackage` (registry.ts:9852) flips the package row and nothing else, `removeActionsByPackage` is called only from `removePackage` and the artifact re-bind, so the disabled package's handler stays in `packageActions`, and `unqualifiedHandler` counts it. For a handler-backed pair with one side disabled, the bare REST and MCP calls resolve the enabled holder's declaration, pass the gates, dispatch unqualified, and the engine answers 409 naming both, the disabled one included. Fail-closed, so no red line is crossed, but the operator's remedy that F4 was about still does not work end to end, and the F4 pin stops at the declaration and never dispatches. I read this off the code and did not run it. Either the engine skips a disabled package's coordinate, or the bare doors dispatch with the holder they resolved; pin it with a dispatch.

**G6 — should-fix, escalated. The built-in entry refuses an authorable name and does not protect the route it cites.** Ruling 2 (b) wanted that "a second holder can never make a platform button 409". `BUILT_IN_BARE_NAMES.action = install_package` (bare-name-one-holder.ts:266) covers the object-less name. The button's route is `/actions/sys_package/install_package`. By this PR's own rule (`hits` is the declarations bound to the routed object first, the object-less ones only when none is bound, action-execution.ts `bareRouteHolderRefusal`), an object-less `install_package` is never reached while `sys_package` binds one, so the entry prevents nothing on that route; and the engine keys `sys_package:install_package` and `global:install_package` apart. The key the button does reach, the object-bound one, is unguarded: two packages binding it are refused by ruling A (the dev's open question), and the census alternative ruling 2 (b) offered ("no package can declare it on that key") is answered in the PR body with "a package can bind an action there". Two more facts the census did not state: both fixed-name callers post to the cloud control plane's URL (cloud-connection-plugin.ts:1409, marketplaceApi.ts:492), and no source in this repository declares the action. So the entry narrows what an author may write for no effect I can find. The epic seat should say which it wants: guard the bound key, or drop the entry and record the census. G5 follows that answer.

**G7 — should-fix. `composeStacks` still refuses the state this PR admits; record it before landing.** `StackComposeActionKeyCollisionError` (packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts:3940, thrown at :8707) refuses two stacks' same object-less action key, with `manifest: 'preserve'` too, and its sentence ("only one of these handlers would be reachable") is no longer true of two namespaces. Closing it is not this PR's to do: it is `packages/spec/src/**`, the spec lane and the schema face, and the card's surface is objectql. It is fail-closed, so no red line is crossed, and the widening is reachable through the install doors. But it means the one first-party way to build a multi-package artifact cannot express the widened state, and the new dogfood reaches it only by editing the composed artifact by hand. Left "to the seat whether it becomes a card" is not a record. Name it on #31527's ledger (or a spec card) in the PR body, as F6 was closed.

**G8 — should-fix. Every bare REST action call now reads two full merged listings, and inherits their failure.** `bareRouteHolderRefusal` runs before every rung (action-execution.ts:5838) and reads the merged `object` and `action` listings on each bare `POST /actions/:object/:action`, collision or not. Before, that door read one schema and one by-name item. Two consequences: a cost on the hot path that the PR does not measure or mention, and the 503 of ① item 4 applying to every bare action call during a listing outage, where an action with one holder ran before. The second is ordered by the epic and is right; it should sit in the BREAKING list with the others, since it is a call that answered and now does not. For the first, say what the read costs on a served kernel (the overlay cache may make it small), or judge from the by-name holders and read the listings only when two are found.

**G5 — should-fix.** The `Metadata-protocol:` token, in ②.

**Nits.**
